title: Creating a Culture of Collaboration
coreMove: Ownership grows when leaders hand real domains to people, give them room to learn, and let their expertise shape the whole experience.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Even the finest dining rooms neglect their ancillary programs, leaving coffee, tea, and cocktails as forgettable afterthoughts at the end of an otherwise extraordinary meal.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Apply the lesson to this situation without copying a surface gesture.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Identifying the people inside the organization most passionate about a given thing and handing them full ownership turns mediocre offerings into world-class ones.

exampleSpecs.stakes: The right moment to give someone real responsibility is often before they feel ready, because being trusted is itself what makes people stretch and grow.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Giving away ownership is harder and slower at the start than keeping control, but it pays off many times over in engagement, quality, and people promoted from within.
